blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.evidence:
export const bucket = (ps: Price[]) =>
  ps.reduce<Record<string, Price[]>>((a, p) => ((a[(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8 ? "hi" : "lo"] ||= []).push(p), a), {});
findings.recommendation: A newcomer reading the docstring "Splits prices into the cheap and the premium ones" cannot recover the premium rule from `(p.cents >> 4) & 0x3e8` without the plan (which says premium means 10 euros and more): a shift, a hex mask and a ternary nested inside an index, inside a `||=`, inside a comma expression in a `reduce` callback. The shape hides what it computes — it is not a threshold at all: 200 cents gives `(200 >> 4) & 0x3e8 === 8`, so a 2-euro price lands in "hi", while 1000 cents lands there too. Rewrite it as a plain loop or two `filter`s on a named constant, e.g. `const PREMIUM_MIN_CENTS = 1000;` and `premium = prices.filter(p => p.cents >= PREMIUM_MIN_CENTS)`, returning a typed `{ cheap: Price[]; premium: Price[] }` instead of a `Record<string, Price[]>` keyed by the magic strings "hi"/"lo" (whose keys are missing when a band is empty); and name it and its parameter for what they are (`splitByPriceBand(prices)` rather than `bucket(ps)`, `a`, `p`).
findings.title: `bucket` packs its premium rule into a bitwise one-liner
